images.description: Boxwork ridges at Murray formation — eroded sulfate veins stand above surrounding mudstone
images.nasaImageId: PLACEHOLDER — replace with real Curiosity Mastcam image ID from mars.nasa.gov/msl/multimedia/raw-images/
images.arrival: On arrival, expect a network of raised ridges (20–50 cm tall) in a reddish-grey mudstone plain. Ridges run roughly parallel, 1–3 m apart. Surface texture is rough; wear-resistant boots needed. The horizon shows a gentle slope rising toward Mount Sharp.

images.description: Glen Torridon clay-bearing outcrop — smooth grey-green mudstone layers
images.nasaImageId: PLACEHOLDER — replace with real Curiosity Mastcam image ID
images.arrival: On arrival, expect grey-green layered mudstone outcrop with smooth, fractured surfaces. Layers are roughly horizontal, 1–5 cm thick. Some surfaces show a slight sheen from clay minerals. The area is relatively flat with low rock relief — good mobility. Dust cover moderate.

images.description: Vera Rubin Ridge hematite outcrop — reddish-grey iron-oxide-bearing rock
images.nasaImageId: PLACEHOLDER — replace with real Curiosity Mastcam image ID
images.arrival: On arrival, expect reddish-grey rock exposed on the ridge crest. Surface is rougher than the clay unit below. Rock outcrops 20–80 cm tall in places. Looking south: the crater floor stretches 2+ km below. Looking north: upslope toward the sulfate unit. Wind-eroded surface with aeolian pits common.

images.description: Gediz Vallis channel — eroded V-shaped valley cutting through sulfate-bearing rock layers
images.nasaImageId: PLACEHOLDER — replace with real Curiosity Navcam image ID
images.arrival: On arrival, expect a broad shallow valley (channel walls 3–8 m tall at this location). Wall exposure shows alternating mudstone and sulfate-rich layers. Rocky debris on the valley floor from erosion. Steep entry to valley floor — approach only via gentle slope. Good cross-section views of Mount Sharp stratigraphy.
